name: Park Hyatt Sydney
positioning: Low-rise harbourside hotel in The Rocks, on the edge of Sydney Harbour facing the Opera House
best_for: Travelers who want a balcony room facing the Sydney Opera House and the harbour
Guests spending New Year's Eve in Sydney who want a view of the harbour fireworks
Families who can share a Double Deluxe Room sleeping up to four

facts.text: The hotel is in The Rocks historic neighborhood on the western side of Sydney Cove.
Circular Quay, a main transportation hub, is about five minutes away on foot.
Bathrooms have a rain shower, bath tub and separate powder room with a heated Toto toilet.
Guest rooms come with Le Labo bath amenities.
The day spa has suite-inspired treatment rooms, a relaxation zone and steam rooms.
The fitness centre overlooks Dawes Point Reserve and Sydney Harbour.
The Dining Room is the hotel's signature restaurant and focuses on locally sourced produce.
The Bar serves cocktails made with native botanicals.
The Living Room offers all-day dining with harbour views through floor-to-ceiling windows.
In-room dining is served by a team of butlers.
Double Deluxe Rooms sleep up to four guests in existing bedding and are suited to families.

highlights.text: Opera View rooms have floor-to-ceiling glass doors opening to a private balcony with direct views of the Sydney Opera House and Sydney Harbour.
The hotel sits on the edge of Sydney Harbour, facing the Sydney Opera House.
The rooftop pool is open year-round with views of Sydney Harbour.
Harbour-facing rooms look out on the New Year's Eve fireworks over the Opera House and Harbour Bridge.
Art commissioned from Australian artists is displayed in the guest rooms and suites.

considerations.text: King Rooms overlook Hickson Road and have no balcony or harbour views.
Getting to city neighborhoods such as Surry Hills and Darlinghurst can feel like a trek.
The better rooms tend to be farther from the elevators, meaning long walks to common spaces.
